## sumtype.md was generated from MiMo v2.5 low reasoning, using the prompt:

> We are planning the addition to the D programming language, and then the implementation thereof, for sumtypes and matching support.
> Existing literature information and some requirements are in the document @plans/sumtype_literature.md
> Your ability to build and test dmd is the bash script @compiler/src/testsumtypematching/run.sh it has instructions in it, for how to run
> the script.
> Write the plan into @plans/sumtype.md

"Should match use method-call syntax `.match!()` (like the literature shows) or a keyword-based syntax `match expr { case ... }`? The
method-call syntax fits D's existing template/UFCS patterns, while keyword syntax is more traditional for pattern matching."

> It should be an expression like context.match { ... }
> It will evaluate to a sumtype for its type.
> Due to match being a valid identifier it should be called __match for the time being.

"Should sumtypes be lowered to structs internally during semantic analysis, or should they have a dedicated `TypeSumType` class throughout
the pipeline?"

> Lower to a struct, but it should derive from that AST class, if there is any additional information that must be kept available.

"Should `None` be a built-in keyword/type, or a library-defined unit type that users create?"

> It should be a library defined type. Possibly an opaque struct ``struct None;``

"What is the MVP scope for the initial implementation?"

> Parse __sumtype declarations, basic match expression, exhaustiveness checking. No niche optimization, no re-tagging
> Use a hash for the tag, not the id of the element, allows the tag to remain the same between instances.
> There will need to be a DIP as per the DIP template in documents, as well as spec changes in spec directory.

"What syntax should `__match` cases use? The literature shows `case int i => expr` but D's existing `case` uses `case exp:`. Which style?"

> `val.__match((int i) => expr, (string s) => expr)` — Lambda-like syntax.
> But it should also support {} like function bodies.

"For the tag hash strategy, how should the hash be computed from the variant types?"

> Hash all variant type names at compile time. Same set of types = same tag values across compilations.

"Should both declaration forms from the literature be supported, or just one?"

> Support both `alias S = __sumtype(int | bool)` and `__sumtype S = int | bool`
> It should also support the longer form declaration so that elements can have names.
> ```d
> __sumtype S {
>     int,
>     bool
> }
> ```

"You mentioned needing a DIP and spec changes. Should these be part of this implementation plan, or separate?"

> Write a DIP document and update spec files as part of this plan

"In the longer form `__sumtype S { ... }`, should variants support optional field names like `int x` for disambiguation when the same type
appears multiple times?"

> Support both named and unnamed forms

"Should match expressions synthesize a sumtype return when arms return different types, as the literature describes?"

> When all arms return type T, result is T. When arms return different types, result is __sumtype(T1 | T2). Enables fluent chaining.

"Should 1-element sumtypes degenerate to aliases as the literature specifies?"

> `__sumtype(int)` lowers to `alias S = int`. Zero overhead, matches the literature.

"What should the `.init` value of a sumtype be?"

> Default to `None` if present, otherwise first variant.

> auto scrutVariant = new DotIdExp(exp.loc, exp.arg, variantField.ident); varientField is corrupted, its pointer is 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF7

> Assigning to an element field is @safe, but reading from that is @system.
> Assigning to a tag is @system, but reading from it is @safe.
> The element storage is opposite of the tag. It is very easy to corrupt the tag by setting it to some random constant like 0 or 42.
> Whereas the element storage cannot be corrupted, the compiler will automaticaly set the tag and if required run the destructor on the old
> value.
> Code that looks like this: ``n.__tag = 0;`` should NEVER EXIST.
> There will need to be a test for structs with destructors and copy constructors as element types.
> To ensure that they can be copied around and the sumtype can be assigned to without corrupting the program.
> Implement both subtyping, auto tag, and running destructor prior to assignment.

> Looking at typesem.d, you are not putting all the varients into an anonymous union, like they should be so that they are overlapping.
> You are generating a hash combining all of the varients types. You should not be doing this.
> Each varient (aka element) get its own hash on its type, to provide it a tag number.
> You should be able to lower assignment to include the destructor call and auto tag assignment.
> Whatever you have done in the past is wrong. It is possible to do this with the help of the comma expression.

## Match not functions

> We need to discuss a previous mistake in the plans for sumtype and matching.
> Matching handlers (the "functions" within the match braces), are not functions.
> They should only support expressions, no block syntax.
> ```d
> st.match {
>     (v) => expr, // ok
>     (v) { // not ok
>         return v;
>     }
> };
> ```
> So we need to remove the function support.
> If we do this, then MatchExp can lower to CondExp and we can remove support for it in e2ir and ctfe engine.
> This was previously not possible due to unsafe access of overlapping fields, but now that DotVar has a flag to say it is safe we can do
> the lowering.

"For the CondExp lowering, should the MatchExp be fully lowered during semantic analysis (in expressionsem.d), so that by the time e2ir/ctfe
see it, it's already a CondExp tree? Or should MatchExp remain as its own node but share a common lowering path?"

> MatchExp semantic replaces the node with CondExp. e2ir, ctfe, and all visitors only see CondExp. Cleanest removal of MatchExp handling
> from e2ir and ctfe.

"For the arm representation in MatchExp, should we change from FuncExp[] to separate body expressions + parameter names, or keep FuncExp[]
and extract in semantic?"

> Change arms from FuncExp[] to VarDeclaration with exp initializer for the expression.

> Parsing must support the storage qualifier ref.
> VarDeclaration can have a type that is null to imply catch all.
> You need to run sumtypematching/run.sh via bash as per the comment for verification and building of dmd.

> You have the example lowering wrong.
> It's going to have to look like ``s.__tag == 0 ? (int x = s.__v0, x * 2)``.
> Due to symbol lookup not having happend when the lowering occurs (and if it had, there would not be any hooks for the arm).
> This will also need to support marking the variable x as ref.
> For the catch all it'll have to copy the variable with initializer, for each varient it thinks could not be handled.
> It has to do a form of exhaustian check, basically if every type and name is present, otherwise the catch all is required. If all present
> its an error to have a catch all.

> There is nothing special about the _ identifier. It is a regular identifier.
> In our case we are supporting a variable declaration without a type. Just like function literals support (and it gets turned into a
> template).
> Also it should be possible if all values are exhaustively handled (which they are required to be), to not need the assert(0) in the
> lowering.
